deep.reconstruction:
Purpose: a proof, by quartic Gauss sums, of biquadratic reciprocity for a complex prime m and a rational prime q ≡ 1 (mod 4). The next page completes this case and starts the case q ≡ 3 (mod 4).

SETUP (top block). Work in Z[i]. Let m be an odd Gaussian prime ('ungerade' is inserted above the line) and m' its conjugate ('Adjuncte'), so N(m) = mm'. The quartic residue symbol [k/m] is the unit in {1, i, -1, -i} with [k/m] ≡ k^{(mm'-1)/4} (mod m). For composite M the symbol (k/M) is the product of [k/m] over all prime factors m of M (Jacobi-type extension).

HYPOTHESES (second block).
- p = mm' is a rational prime ≡ 1 (mod 4).
- q is a rational prime ≠ p with q = nn'. The deleted words show q ≡ 1 (mod 4) is the case being treated.
- Normalization (margin): the real parts of m and n are ≡ 1 (mod 4).
- x is an indeterminate and X = (x^p - 1)/(x - 1). Working mod X means working in Z[i][ζ] with ζ a primitive p-th root of unity.
- e is a primitive root mod m (equivalently mod p) chosen so that e^{(p-1)/4} ≡ i (mod m), i.e. χ(e) = i, where χ = [·/m].

DEFINITIONS (modern form).
- T = Σ_{j=0}^{p-2} i^j x^{e^j}. Since i^j = χ(e^j), this is T = Σ_{k=1}^{p-1} χ(k) ζ^k = G(χ), the quartic Gauss sum.
- U = Σ_j i^j x^{q e^j} = Σ_k χ(k) ζ^{qk}.
- V = Σ_j (-1)^j x^{e^j} = Σ_k (k/p) ζ^k = G(χ²), the quadratic Gauss sum.

STEP 1: T² ≡ -mV (mod X). In modern terms G(χ)² = J(χ,χ)·G(χ²), and with Gauss's normalization (Re m ≡ 1 mod 4) the Jacobi sum is J(χ,χ) = -m. Gauss justifies this from the multiplication of periods (Disq. Arith. art. 345) together with the cyclotomic numbers of order 4 (Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum I, arts. 18–20), which give the decomposition p = a² + b².

STEP 2: V² ≡ p (mod X). This is G(χ²)² = (-1/p)·p = p, since p ≡ 1 (mod 4).

STEP 3 (follows from 1 and 2): T⁴ ≡ m²V² ≡ m²p = m³m' (mod X).

STEP 4: T^q ≡ U (mod q). This is the Frobenius/multinomial congruence (Σa_k)^q ≡ Σa_k^q (mod q), cited as Disq. Arith. art. 53. It needs χ(k)^q = χ(k), i.e. q ≡ 1 (mod 4); the struck-out remark recorded exactly this.

STEP 5: (q/m)·U ≡ T (mod X). Substitute k → qk: U = Σ χ(k)ζ^{qk} = χ(q)^{-1} Σ χ(k')ζ^{k'} = χ(q)^{-1} T.

STEP 6 (struck through, then replaced): χ(q)T^q ≡ T, hence χ(q)T^{q-1} ≡ 1 (mod X, q). The cancellation of T needs T to be invertible mod (q, X). Gauss's deleted justification spoke of common factors x - r. A cleaner argument (mine): T·T³ ≡ m³m', which is prime to q, so T is a unit mod q.

STEP 7: Combining the three statements as in the 1818 paper (sixth proof of quadratic reciprocity, art. 6): raise T⁴ ≡ m³m' to the power (q-1)/4. This gives χ(q)·(m³m')^{(q-1)/4} ≡ 1 (mod q). Both sides lie in Z[i], and Z[i][x]/(X) is free over Z[i], so the congruence descends to Z[i] (my remark). Hence it holds mod n and mod n'.

NEXT PAGE (context, completing the argument).
- Mod n this reads (q/m)[m/n]³[m'/n] = 1, so (q/m)[m'/n] = [m/n]; similarly mod n'.
- Since [m'/n][m/n'] = 1, multiplying gives (q/m) = [m/n][m/n'] = (m/q).
- This is biquadratic reciprocity for a primary complex prime and a rational prime q ≡ 1 (mod 4).
errors: No mathematical error found in the retained lines. I checked T² = -mV and T⁴ = m³m' for p = 5, m = 1+2i (J(χ,χ) = -1-2i = -m). With Gauss's normalization 'real part ≡ 1 (mod 4)', J(χ,χ) = -m holds for both p ≡ 1 and p ≡ 5 (mod 8). This differs from the modern 'primary' convention (Ireland–Rosen: J = -χ(-1)π), but it is consistent.

Cancelling T in χ(q)T^q ≡ T (mod X, q) needs T to be invertible mod q. Gauss's first justification (no common factor x - r of X and T) was struck out, and the final text just says 'folgt leicht'. The gap is easily filled because T⁴ ≡ m³m' is prime to q.
The citation 'Disq. Arith. art. 53' for (a+b+...)^q ≡ a^q+b^q+... is probably a slip or misreading. The multinomial congruence is art. 51.
The hypothesis q ≡ 1 (mod 4) is needed in steps 4–7 but survives only in deleted text and in the next page's 'zweite Fall'. The page as it stands states it only implicitly.

results.what: Quartic residue symbol [k/m] ≡ k^{(N m - 1)/4} (mod m), extended multiplicatively to composite moduli
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum, 1828/1832); composite extension in Jacobi/Eisenstein style

results.what: G(χ)² = J(χ,χ)·G(χ²) with J(χ,χ) = -m (normalization Re m ≡ 1 mod 4), hence G(χ)⁴ = m³m' = p·m²
results.modern_name: Quartic Gauss sum evaluation via Jacobi sums (G(χ)⁴ = pJ(χ,χ)²)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (letters/lectures 1827–1837), Eisenstein (1844); Gauss's cyclotomic numbers of order 4 (1828) supply the input

results.what: Proof of [q/m] = [m/q] for a primary Gaussian prime m and a rational prime q ≡ 1 (mod 4), via Frobenius on the quartic Gauss sum
results.modern_name: Biquadratic reciprocity (mixed case) proved by Gauss sums
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1836–37 Königsberg lectures, unpublished) and Eisenstein (1844, Crelle); Gauss announced but never published a proof

results.what: T^q ≡ U (mod q) and χ(q)U = T, giving χ(q) ≡ G^{-(q-1)} (mod q)
results.modern_name: Frobenius congruence for Gauss sums (as in the sixth proof of quadratic reciprocity)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, essentially complete Gauss-sum proof of a case of biquadratic reciprocity. It uses exactly the method later published by Eisenstein (1844) and lectured on by Jacobi (1836–37). Gauss claimed to have a proof but published none, and his Nachlass is known to contain fragments on the subject (some printed in Werke II/X). So this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a priority upset. I am unsure whether this specific sheet has already been edited.

Deleted remark after 'T^q ≡ U (mod q)' appears to read '(wenn q ≡ 1 mod 4)', not 'wenn q = ... 4'.
Second hypothesis line: 'von p verschieden, [-und-] ≡ nn'' — the '≡' is written above the line as an insertion ('= nn''); the struck text 'im Fall wo q ≡ 1 (mod 4)' is deleted.
'Disqu. Arithm. art. 53' is as written, but the intended reference is likely art. 51 (multinomial congruence mod a prime).
